discovery: The optical lattice clock: magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms enabling optical frequency standards at the 10^-18 level

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock (2001-2005): trapping thousands of neutral atoms at a 'magic' wavelength where the light shift cancels, breaking the prevailing view that strong trapping fields must perturb the clock transition. This combined the Lamb-Dicke confinement of ion clocks with the statistical power of many atoms. Jun Ye, building on the frequency-comb revolution, developed ultrastable lasers, many-body control and comb-based readout that brought strontium lattice clocks to systematic uncertainties near 10^-18 and resolved the gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample. Lattice clocks now outperform the caesium standard by two orders of magnitude, are driving the redefinition of the SI second, enable chronometric geodesy, and serve as sensitive probes of dark matter and variations of fundamental constants. This is precision measurement transformed into a new tool for fundamental physics.
